questions.text: Explain how tokens are generated by the lexical analyzer phase of a compiler using Finite Automata. Describe how a syntax analyzer uses Context-Free Grammars to construct parse trees for expressions like $r = a + b * c / (d * e)$.
State and prove the Pumping Lemma for Regular Languages. Use it to prove that the languages $L = \{0^n 1^n \mid n \ge 0\}$ and $L = \{a^p \mid p \text{ is a prime number}\}$ are not regular.
questions.solutionOutline: If L is regular, exists pumping length p such that any s in L with |s| >= p can be written s = xyz with: 1) |y| > 0; 2) |xy| <= p; 3) x y^i z in L for all i >= 0. For 0^p 1^p, y consists purely of 0s. Pumping i=2 gives string with more 0s than 1s, contradiction. For a^p, choosing i = p+1 yields composite length p + y*p = p(1+y), contradiction.

questions.chapter: Context Free Grammar and Pushdown Automata
questions.text: State and prove the Pumping Lemma for Context-Free Languages (CFL). Use it to prove that the language $L = \{a^n b^n c^n \mid n \ge 1\}$ is not context-free.
questions.solutionOutline: For CFL L, exists pumping length p such that any s in L with |s| >= p can be split s = uvwxy with: 1) |vx| > 0; 2) |vwx| <= p; 3) u v^i w x^i y in L for all i >= 0. For s = a^p b^p c^p, the substring vwx can contain at most two distinct symbols because |vwx| <= p. Pumping i=2 increases counts of at most two symbol types, violating equal count condition of a, b, c.

questions.text: Convert a given Non-Deterministic Finite Automaton with epsilon-transitions (\epsilon-NFA) to an equivalent Deterministic Finite Automaton (DFA) using the subset construction algorithm with $\epsilon$-closure calculations.
questions.solutionOutline: 1) Compute epsilon-closure of start state q0 as initial DFA state Q0; 2) For each DFA state S and input symbol a, compute next state delta_DFA(S, a) = epsilon-closure(delta_NFA(S, a)); 3) Add newly discovered subsets to state table until no new states are generated; 4) Any subset containing an accepting state of NFA is designated as an accepting state in DFA.

questions.text: Minimize a given DFA using the Table-Filling Algorithm (Myhill-Nerode theorem equivalence partitioning). Show the step-by-step marking of distinguishability pairs and construct the minimal state DFA.
questions.solutionOutline: 1) Draw table for all unordered pairs {p, q}; 2) Mark all pairs where one is accepting and other non-accepting; 3) Iteratively mark unmarked pair {p, q} if for some input a, {delta(p,a), delta(q,a)} is already marked; 4) Repeat until no new pairs are marked; 5) Unmarked pairs are equivalent and merged into single equivalence states in minimal DFA.

questions.chapter: Context Free Grammar and Pushdown Automata
questions.text: Convert a given Context-Free Grammar (CFG) into Chomsky Normal Form (CNF) step-by-step: elimination of $\epsilon$-productions, elimination of unit productions ($A \to B$), elimination of useless symbols, and restructuring into $A \to BC$ and $A \to a$.
questions.solutionOutline: CNF format requires productions of form A -> BC or A -> a. Steps: 1) Eliminate nullable epsilon-productions; 2) Eliminate unit productions A -> B using unit pairs; 3) Eliminate useless non-generating and unreachable symbols; 4) Replace terminals in mixed productions with auxiliary variables; 5) Break long productions of 3+ variables into cascade of binary productions.

questions.chapter: Context Free Grammar and Pushdown Automata
questions.text: Convert a given Context-Free Grammar (CFG) into Greibach Normal Form (GNF) where all production rules are of the form $A \to a \alpha$ with $a \in \Sigma$ and $\alpha \in V^*$. Explain the elimination of left recursion using auxiliary variables.
questions.solutionOutline: Order variables A1, A2, ..., An. Ensure i < j for productions Ai -> Aj gamma. Eliminate immediate left recursion Ai -> Ai alpha | beta by introducing auxiliary variable B: Ai -> beta | beta B, and B -> alpha | alpha B. Back-substitute from An down to A1 so every rule begins with a terminal symbol.

questions.chapter: Context Free Grammar and Pushdown Automata
questions.text: Explain the equivalence between Acceptance by Final State ($L(M)$) and Acceptance by Empty Stack ($N(M)$) in Pushdown Automata. Provide constructive algorithms to convert a PDA from one acceptance criterion to the other.
questions.solutionOutline: Both define exactly class of CFLs. N(M) to L(M'): add new start state pushing bottom marker Z0 and entering M start state; add new final state qf; from any state of M encountering empty stack marker Z0, transition to qf. L(M) to N(M''): from any final state of M, non-deterministically branch to an erasing state that empties stack completely.

questions.text: Design a Turing Machine that computes the 2's complement of a given binary string or multiplies a unary number by 2 ($f(1^n) = 1^{2n}$). Provide the formal 7-tuple definition, transition table, and trace tape transitions for sample input.
questions.solutionOutline: 2s complement algorithm: 1) Scan right to rightmost bit; 2) Scan left leaving trailing 0s unchanged until encountering first 1 (leave first 1 unchanged); 3) Continue scanning left, inverting all remaining bits (0->1, 1->0). Formal tuple M = (Q, Sigma, Gamma, delta, q0, B, F) with state transitions and tape head movements.

questions.text: Explain the Church-Turing Thesis and the concept of a Universal Turing Machine (UTM). How does a UTM simulate any arbitrary Turing Machine $M$ on input $w$ using binary encoding of states and tape transitions?
questions.solutionOutline: Church-Turing Thesis posits that any algorithmic calculation executable by humans or physical computers can be computed by a Turing Machine. UTM is a single fixed TM that takes description <M> and input w on its multi-track tape: Track 1 stores encoding <M>, Track 2 stores current tape of M, Track 3 stores current state of M. Faithfully simulates transition step-by-step.

questions.text: Define the Halting Problem of Turing Machines. Prove that the Halting Problem $H_{TM} = \{\langle M, w \rangle \mid M \text{ halts on input } w\}$ is undecidable using proof by contradiction and Cantor's diagonalization method.
questions.solutionOutline: Assume decider H exists: H(<M, w>) accepts if M halts on w, rejects if M loops. Construct machine D(<M>): runs H(<M, <M>>); if H accepts, D loops infinitely; if H rejects, D halts. Now evaluate D(<D>): if D halts, H accepts => D loops; if D loops, H rejects => D halts. Contradiction proves decider H cannot exist.

questions.text: Explain the Post Correspondence Problem (PCP) and Modified Post Correspondence Problem (MPCP). Prove that PCP is undecidable by reduction from the Halting Problem or TM Acceptance problem.
questions.solutionOutline: Given two lists of strings A = (x1, ..., xk) and B = (y1, ..., yk). PCP asks if there exists index sequence i1, i2, ..., im such that xi1 xi2 ... xim = yi1 yi2 ... yim. MPCP requires i1 = 1. Undecidability proved by reducing TM acceptance problem A_TM to MPCP: matching string tiles simulates valid computation history of TM; MPCP reduces to PCP.

questions.text: State and explain Rice's Theorem on recursive and recursively enumerable languages. Use Rice's Theorem to show that determining whether $L(M) = \emptyset$ or whether $L(M)$ is regular are undecidable problems.
questions.solutionOutline: Rice Theorem states that any non-trivial semantic property of recursively enumerable languages is undecidable. Property P is non-trivial if at least one RE language satisfies P and at least one does not. Emptiness (L(M) = empty) and regularity are properties of language recognized by M (semantic) and non-trivial; hence both are undecidable by direct application of Rice theorem.

questions.chapter: Introduction to Formal Language, Logic and Proof
questions.text: Explain the Chomsky Hierarchy of Formal Languages: Type-0 (Unrestricted), Type-1 (Context-Sensitive), Type-2 (Context-Free), and Type-3 (Regular). List their defining grammar formats, accepting automata, and closure properties under union, intersection, and complementation.
questions.solutionOutline: Type-3: Regular Grammars, Finite Automata, closed under union, intersection, complement. Type-2: Context-Free Grammars (A -> gamma), Pushdown Automata, closed under union, concatenation, Kleene star, not intersection/complement. Type-1: Context-Sensitive Grammars (alpha A beta -> alpha gamma beta), Linear Bounded Automata, closed under all Boolean operations. Type-0: Unrestricted Grammars, Turing Machines, closed under union, intersection, not complement.

questions.text: Define complexity classes P, NP, NP-Complete, and NP-Hard. Explain polynomial-time reduction ($A \le_p B$) and state the Cook-Levin Theorem proving that the Boolean Satisfiability problem (SAT / 3-SAT) is NP-Complete.
questions.solutionOutline: P is class of decision problems solvable in deterministic polynomial time. NP is solvable in nondeterministic polynomial time (verifiable in polynomial time). Problem X is NP-Complete if X in NP and for every Y in NP, Y <=_p X. Cook-Levin theorem proved SAT is NP-Complete by showing any nondeterministic TM computation of polynomial length can be encoded as a Boolean formula in CNF.
